summary: This CSS defines styling for logo elements in a presentation framework (likely Reveal.js). It positions logos in different locations on slides—one in the bottom-right corner with a height constraint, another in the top-left with a fixed pixel size—and ensures they display as fixed elements that don't get constrained by normal width limits.

explanations.3: unset removes any inherited or previously-set left positioning so the element isn't pulled to the left side.
explanations.5: max-height limits how tall the logo can grow, even if its container is larger, keeping it at a reasonable 2.2rem size.
explanations.6: right: 12px positions the element 12 pixels away from the right edge of the screen.
explanations.10: unset removes the bottom positioning so this logo variant can use top positioning instead.
explanations.13: max-height: unset removes any height restrictions so this logo can use its full 100px height without being capped.
explanations.21: position: fixed makes the logo stay in place relative to the viewport even when scrolling, rather than moving with the content.
explanations.22: width: 100x is likely a typo—should probably be 100% or 100px—but with unset max-width, the element's width isn't artificially constrained.
